rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent terraced mass with a clear dominant gesture, and it survives across the four views without obvious view-to-view collisions. The top view shows a parcel-responsive oblique/terraced footprint rather than a generic box fill, and the blue frontage edge is answered by an entry notch/seam rather than a sealed wall, so the access relation is plausible. Programmatically, a compact neighborhood-living building can support this massing because it offers an active ground threshold, a usable void/entry cut, and calmer stepped upper massing. The main weakness is that the stepped form still leans somewhat toward repetitive tiering, with section logic that is serviceable but not exceptional; it reads as a competent neighborhood terrace rather than a strongly articulated inhabited section. Still, it is within the program envelope and not typologically wrong.
